# Thin-edge endpoint fibers obstruct universal individual best-menu Gamma efficiency

Status: independently audited PASS in \`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)\` and \`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)\`. This is an auxiliary obstruction, NOT an OC counterexample. It disproves a universal individual-source efficiency lemma even after optimizing over ALL actual positive-width active menus and ALL nonnegative normal-dependent convex physical fields. The example has one heavy middle fiber and is far above the OC target.

We use \(n=1,d=4\), the first dimension in which
\[
2/5<\Gamma_4=(4/5)^4=256/625.
\]
All assertions below hold for a sufficiently small FIXED \(\delta>0\), followed by every sufficiently small positive outward width \(h\). No numerical optimization is used.

## 1. Dependencies and their precise uses

We use the already proved ordinary simplex facts: its maximum depth is \(\Gamma_4\), its unique deepest point is its centroid, and its only least-volume through-centroid cap normals are the five vertex-isolating facet-parallel directions. The all-normal classification appears in
\`candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c\`.
Compactness then gives a strict normal gap outside any fixed neighborhoods of these five normals.

We use the cap differentiability, actual attained active normals, finite clipping, and full-normal kernel moment identity of
\`candidate 6e754f2bf13bdbd1\`.
For the explicit family below, proper source cores and a pure-base gap are verified directly before these facts are used.

Two ordinary convex-functional facts on a 3-simplex facet are used, both proved in the cited sources:
* \`candidate 81d65baa0f0a1024\` gives, for convex \(f\geq0\) vanishing at the facet centroid,
  \[
  \int W_0f\leq \Gamma_4(1-c_4)\int f,\qquad
  c_4=7/320,\quad \Gamma_4c_4=28/3125, \tag{1}
  \]
  where \(W_0=(1/5)\sum_{j\ne i}1_{\{\lambda_j\geq1/5\}}\) on facet \(F_i\).
* The elementary weighted-strip proof in Section2 of
  \`candidate c62d1cc13c75171f\` gives
  \[
  \int_{\{|\lambda_j-1/5|\leq t\}} f\leq40t\int f \tag{2}
  \]
  for sufficiently small \(t\), every nonnegative convex \(f\), uniformly even when its mass concentrates near facet boundaries.

The simplex facet mass/first-moment identity used below is derived again in Section5. No mixed-integer Grünbaum bound, unknown density theorem, or stationary-body separator is assumed.

## 2. The actual convex family

Let \(T\) be a regular 4-simplex centered at the origin, with barycentrics
\(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_4\), volume \(V\), and centroid \(g\). Set
\[
J=\{0,1\},\qquad
D_\delta=\{x\in T:\lambda_2+\lambda_3+\lambda_4\leq\delta\},
\quad 0<\delta<1/10.
\]
Use fibers
\[
K_0=T,\qquad K_{-1}=K_1=D_\delta.
\]
Their canonical convex hull has exactly these three integer fibers: the endpoint bodies coincide and lie in \(T\). It is a full-dimensional convex body in \(\mathbb R^5\).

Under uniform simplex volume, \(R=\lambda_2+\lambda_3+\lambda_4\) has density \(12r^2(1-r)\). This follows by separating its three-coordinate and two-coordinate barycentric simplexes; their slice factors are \(r^2\) and \(1-r\), and normalization gives twelve. Hence
\[
\alpha:=|D_\delta|/V=4\delta^3-3\delta^4. \tag{3}
\]
The pooled within-fiber covariance \(\Sigma_\delta\) tends to the positive covariance of \(T\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). Indeed the middle contribution has fixed positive mass and the endpoint second moments are uniformly bounded while their masses tend to zero. Use the actual covariance norm \(\Gamma_\delta\) and the buffer-free uniform outward CDF \(\Psi(t)=\min(1,\max(0,1+t))\).

The body is invariant under the permutations within \(J\) and within \(J^c\), acting orthogonally on the regular simplex. These symmetries preserve its pooled covariance, all ambient halfspaces, and the actual smoothed objective.

## 3. Every active cap belongs to one of five vertex cones

Write \(Q_{\delta,h}\) for maximal raw smooth depth. At the middle centroid, every nonvertical cap includes its ordinary through-centroid middle cap; pure-base caps contain the entire middle fiber. Thus
\[
Q_{\delta,h}\geq\Gamma_4V.
\]
At any middle mark and in any continuous direction, a sufficiently large finite base tilt captures exactly one whole endpoint and misses the other. Therefore the middle mixed depth is at most its ordinary own depth plus \(\alpha V+C h\), where the uniform slab bound gives one constant \(C\) for this fixed bounded family and its uniformly positive covariance norms. At an exposed endpoint base the own cap can be isolated, so its maximal depth is at most \(\alpha V<\Gamma_4V\).

Every deepest source is consequently at base zero. The canonical own caps \(\lambda_i\geq\lambda_i(y)\) have fractions \((1-\lambda_i(y))^4\). The preceding estimates imply that, as \(\delta,h\downarrow0\), every deepest middle mark tends uniformly to \(g\). More explicitly, \((1-\max_i\lambda_i(y))^4\geq\Gamma_4-\alpha-Ch/V\), and the coordinate sum is one. This bounds each coordinate difference from \(1/5\) by \(C'(\alpha+h)\).

The source therefore lies in a fixed own core. All width strips through it are proper when \(h\) is small, and pure-base caps have mass at least \(V+\alpha V\), separated from \(Q_{\delta,h}\leq\Gamma_4V+\alpha V+Ch\). Thus active nonvertical caps are attained, with positive own coarea. The C1 full-normal identity implies uniqueness of the middle deepest mark: an active cap at a midpoint of two distinct deepest marks would be the same active cap at both, forcing equality of their effective kernel centroids. Denote the unique source by \(Y_h=(0,y_h)\).

For an active cap, its ordinary own through-\(y_h\) mass is at most \(Q_{\delta,h}\). The ordinary simplex normal gap and compactness of normalized continuous directions now show that every active continuous normal lies in arbitrarily small fixed disjoint cones about the five canonical vertex directions, provided \(\delta,h\) are sufficiently small. Each such cap strictly isolates the corresponding vertex on the middle fiber. This statement covers ALL base tilts.

Choose the five cones so small that any continuous positive balance uses every cone. This is possible because zero lies outside the convex hull of any four canonical normalized normals, with a positive finite gap; small neighborhoods preserve that separation. We fix these cones once and then shrink \(\delta,h\) as needed.

## 4. Exact outside costs and vanishing outside coarea for ALL active caps

Consider first an active direction in a cone with index \(i\notin J\). Its margin at the source is a small perturbation of \(\lambda_i(x)-\lambda_i(y_h)\). On \(D_\delta\), \(\lambda_i(x)\leq\delta\), whereas \(\lambda_i(y_h)\) is near \(1/5\). Zero base tilt therefore makes both endpoint integrands identically zero, with a fixed strict margin beyond the small smoothing strip. Actual minimality in the base tilt forces every active cap in this cone to have outside mass zero. It also forces zero endpoint strip coarea.

For a direction in the cone at \(i=0\) or \(i=1\), let \(R_J\) swap barycentric coordinates zero and one. It preserves \(D_\delta\) and its volume. The sum of the through-source continuous margins of \(x\) and \(R_Jx\), for the canonical index-zero direction, is
\[
\lambda_0(x)+\lambda_1(x)-2\lambda_0(y_h)
\geq1-\delta-2\lambda_0(y_h).
\]
This is uniformly positive. The same remains true throughout both sufficiently small cones, by compactness, uniformly on \(D_\delta\). In a pair of endpoint points \((-1,x),(1,R_Jx)\), the base-tilt contributions cancel. Consequently for EVERY base tilt the paired smooth captures sum to at least one, and their integrated outside mass is at least \(|D_\delta|\).

A finite large tilt attains exactly \(|D_\delta|\), by capturing one endpoint entirely and missing the other. Thus every actually active cap in either J-cone has outside mass exactly \(|D_\delta|\). Moreover both endpoint strip coareas vanish. To verify the last point, if one member of a paired point has a strictly intermediate kernel value, the uniform positive sum of margins puts its paired member strictly in the fully captured regime. Their capture sum is then strictly greater than one. A positive transition-strip volume would therefore make the integrated mass strictly greater than \(|D_\delta|\), which is impossible.

We have proved, for ALL actual active caps,
\[
Q^{\rm out}_i=\alpha V\,1_{\{i\in J\}},\qquad
S^{\rm out}_i=0. \tag{4}
\]
For any response menu, its endpoint boundary profile is bounded pointwise by the total response weight \(\nu(J)\) carried by the two J-cones. No choice of their base tilts can violate this bound.

## 5. The unique limiting source, caps, and menu weights

Fix a sufficiently small positive \(\delta\) and let \(h\downarrow0\). Source marks stay in a compact core, and continuous active normals stay in the five fixed cones. Since all coarea is own, the actual full-normal identity says that each own strip centroid differs from \(y_h\) by at most \(C h\). Every limiting proper own section therefore has centroid \(y\), the limiting source.

A vertex-i section of a simplex has centroid \(y\) exactly when its edge intercepts from vertex i are \(4y_k\), \(k\ne i\). Thus the cap within each cone is uniquely determined by y. Every balanced menu uses all five cones, so there is an active cap in every cone. The common raw cap mass and (4) imply
\[
q_i+\alpha 1_{\{i\in J\}}=q,\qquad
q_i=4^4\prod_k y_k/y_i. \tag{5}
\]
Uniqueness of the positive-width source and the actual permutation symmetries give equal coordinates within J and within its complement. Write these as \(x\) and \(z\). Then
\[
2x+3z=1,\qquad
256xz^2(x-z)=\alpha. \tag{6}
\]
The solution near \(x=z=1/5\) is unique for small \(\alpha\). Indeed put \(x=1/5+s,\ z=1/5-2s/3\); the left side of the second equation is a polynomial \(F(s)\) with \(F(0)=0,\ F'(0)=256/75>0\). On a fixed sufficiently small interval its derivative is at least \(128/75\). The intermediate value theorem therefore gives the unique small positive solution and \(s\leq(75/128)\alpha\).

Every subsequential limit is this same solution, so the source and the cone-wise continuous active directions converge uniformly. Normalize own coareas consistently. The limiting response balance has its unique positive weights
\[
r_i=1-4y_i,\qquad
\theta_i=\frac{r_i/q_i}{B},\qquad B=\sum_jr_j/q_j. \tag{7}
\]
One direct derivation is to differentiate the vertex-cap fraction at its section-centroid configuration. If \(T_0=\sum_i\theta_iq_i\), balance on the barycentric-sum-one tangent space gives \(\theta_iq_i=T_0(1-4y_i)\); normalization gives (7). All \(r_i\) are positive near the uniform source.

Every actual menu, including one with multiple caps in a cone, has cone-total response weights tending uniformly to (7). Otherwise a contrary sequence has a limiting probability vector balancing the limiting five response normals but different from their unique normalized dependence. Thus
\[
\sup_{\text{actual menus}}\nu(J)\longrightarrow\theta_0+\theta_1
\longrightarrow2/5\quad\text{as first }h\downarrow0,\ \delta\downarrow0.
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\) and then small h, we may and do require
\[
\Gamma_4-\nu(J)\geq g_0:=3/625>0 \tag{8}
\]
for EVERY active response menu.

On source facet \(F_i\), the limiting profile \(W_\delta\) has exact mass and first moments equal to \(\beta_\delta\) times uniform facet area, where
\[
\beta_\delta=1/B.
\]
Indeed cap j, \(j\ne i\), occupies area fraction \(q_j/(4y_i)\), has facet centroid with coordinate \(y_k\) for \(k\ne i,j\), and coordinate \(y_i+y_j\) at j. Consequently its weighted total facet mass is \((1-r_i)/(4By_i)=1/B\), and each remaining barycentric first moment is
\[
y_k/B+r_k/(4B)=1/(4B).
\]
Thus
\[
\int_{F_i}(W_\delta-\beta_\delta)\ell=0
\quad\text{for EVERY affine }\ell. \tag{9}
\]

The explicit rational formula is
\[
\beta_\delta=\frac{4^4\prod_i y_i}{1-4\sum_i y_i^2}.
\]
It is smooth near the uniform point, has zero first derivative on the coordinate-sum-one tangent space by permutation symmetry, and equals \(\Gamma_4\) there. Its second derivatives are bounded on a fixed compact neighborhood with positive denominator. Twice integrating those bounded derivatives along the segment from the uniform point, and using \(s=O(\alpha)\), proves
\[
|\beta_\delta-\Gamma_4|\leq C_1\alpha^2. \tag{10}
\]
Only this upper bound is needed.

## 6. Uniform source-facet coercivity, including concentrating convex fields

On a source facet use normalized facet area. If \(f\geq0\) is convex and vanishes at its centroid, (1) gives a fixed canonical gap \(28/3125\). The limiting source barycentrics, cap plane coefficients, and response weights differ from the canonical ones by \(O(\alpha)\). Each changed cap lies between two parallel canonical planes whose barycentric thresholds differ by \(C\alpha\). Thus (2), together with the weight change, bounds the change of \(\int W f\) by \(C_2\alpha\int f\). At positive width the same statement holds with an additional quantity tending uniformly to zero over all active menus. Choose \(\delta\), then h, sufficiently small to obtain
\[
\int W_h f\leq(\Gamma_4-\kappa)\int f,\qquad
\kappa:=14/3125. \tag{11}
\]
The estimate is uniform over every nonnegative convex f. No bounded ratio of its supremum to its integral is assumed.

Now let \(\phi\geq0\) be any continuous convex function on the facet, and choose a supporting affine function \(\ell\) at its centroid. Put \(f=\phi-\ell\geq0\), so \(f\) vanishes there, and write
\[
I=\int\phi,\qquad \varepsilon=\int f,\qquad
\int\ell=\ell(g_F)=\phi(g_F)\geq0.
\]
There is a dimension-only bound
\[
\sup_F|\ell|\leq3072 I. \tag{12}
\]
To prove it, write \(\ell=\sum_{k=1}^4c_k\lambda_k\). Its mean is nonnegative. If \(M=\max c_k>0\), every coefficient is at least \(-3M\). On the corner simplex \(\lambda_{\max}\geq7/8\), of area fraction \(1/512\), \(\ell\geq M/2\). Since \(\phi\geq\ell_+\), \(I\geq M/1024\), proving (12). If \(M=0\), all coefficients vanish.

The actual profiles converge in facet \(L^1\) to \(W_\delta\), uniformly over all menus, by the uniform convergence of cone-wise caps and weights proved in Section5; their limiting cut boundaries have facet area zero. Combining (9) and (12) yields a number \(e_\delta(h)\downarrow0\) such that
\[
\left|\int(W_h-W_\delta)\ell\right|\leq e_\delta(h)I.
\]
Together with (10)--(11), this proves the central bound
\[
\int(W_h-\Gamma_4)\phi
\leq [C_1\alpha^2+e_\delta(h)]I-\kappa\varepsilon. \tag{13}
\]
This is uniform over the entire convex test cone, including unboundedly steep sequences of normalized tests.

## 7. An elementary affine-observability estimate on every shared patch

Let \(A_i=D_\delta\cap F_i\). On every source facet choose a vertex \(e_j\) with \(j\in J\setminus\{i\}\). The simplex
\[
E_i=(1-\delta/2)e_j+(\delta/2)
           [\,g_{F_i}/2+F_i/2\,]
\]
lies in \(A_i\), has normalized facet area \(\delta^3/64\), and every one of its four facet barycentric coordinates is at least \(\delta/16\).

For an arbitrary affine function \(\ell\) on \(F_i\) with mean \(s>0\), we claim
\[
\int\ell_-+\int_{A_i}\ell_+\geq2^{-23}\delta^4s. \tag{14}
\]
Divide by s. Its four vertex coefficients now sum to four. Put
\(\eta=\max(0,-\min c_k)\); their maximum is at most \(4+3\eta\).

If \(\eta\leq\delta/8\), then on \(E_i\)
\[
\ell=\sum_k(c_k+\eta)\lambda_k-\eta
\geq(\delta/16)(4+4\eta)-\eta\geq\delta/8.
\]
Hence the second integral in (14) is at least \(\delta^4/512\).

If \(\eta>\delta/8\), take a vertex of value \(-\eta\). In its corner simplex of scale \(\eta/[2(M+\eta)]\), the affine value is at most \(-\eta/2\). Thus
\[
\int\ell_-\geq\frac{\eta^4}{16(M+\eta)^3}
\geq\frac{\eta^4}{1024(1+\eta)^3}
\geq2^{-23}\delta^4.
\]
The last inequality uses \(\delta\leq1\) and the increasing function
\(\eta^4/(1+\eta)^3\). This proves (14).

For the supporting function and remainder in Section6, \(f\geq\ell_-\) and \(\phi\geq\ell_+\). If \(J_i=\int_{A_i}\phi\), (14) gives
\[
\varepsilon+J_i\geq2^{-23}\delta^4(I-\varepsilon).
\]
If \(I-\varepsilon=0\), the following consequence is immediate; otherwise rearrange. In either case,
\[
\varepsilon+J_i\geq2^{-24}\delta^4 I. \tag{15}
\]
This estimate is the reason fields concentrating away from the tiny shared patch do not evade the argument: doing so creates a quantified nonaffine source deficit.

## 8. The whole ambient convex-field cone has efficiency STRICTLY below Gamma

Let \(\Phi(n,z,x)\geq0\) be ANY globally finite continuous physical field convex in \((z,x)\) for each normal n. Let \(D_\Phi\) denote its total boundary integral, and \(N_\Phi\) its integral against the selected source's response profile. We allow ANY balanced actual active response menu.

At the source facet normal \(n_i\), set \(\phi_i(x)=\Phi(n_i,0,x)\). On its common endpoint patches, convexity in the base variable gives
\[
2\phi_i(x)\leq\Phi(n_i,-1,x)+\Phi(n_i,1,x),
\qquad x\in A_i.
\]
Therefore the endpoint boundary integral, denoted \(E_\Phi\), satisfies
\[
E_\Phi\geq2\sum_i |F_i|\int_{A_i}\phi_i. \tag{16}
\]
Edges have zero facet measure. Additional truncation facets of the endpoints only increase \(E_\Phi\).

By (4),(8), the entire endpoint profile is at most \(\Gamma_4-g_0\). Combining this with (13) gives
\[
N_\Phi-\Gamma_4D_\Phi
\leq\sum_i|F_i|
  \{[C_1\alpha^2+e_\delta(h)]I_i-\kappa\varepsilon_i\}
  -g_0E_\Phi.
\]
Use half the endpoint term in (16), and retain the other half. Since
\(\kappa<g_0\), (15) gives
\[
N_\Phi-\Gamma_4D_\Phi
\leq[C_1\alpha^2+e_\delta(h)-c_*\delta^4]
       \sum_i|F_i|I_i-\frac{g_0}{2}E_\Phi,\qquad
c_*=\kappa\,2^{-24}>0. \tag{17}
\]
Because \(\alpha\leq4\delta^3\), choose fixed \(\delta>0\) so small that all earlier conditions hold and
\(16C_1\delta^6\leq c_*\delta^4/4\).
Then choose h small enough for all earlier conditions and
\(e_\delta(h)\leq c_*\delta^4/4\).
Equation (17) proves, for EVERY field and EVERY menu,
\[
N_\Phi\leq(\Gamma_4-\zeta_\delta)D_\Phi,\qquad
\zeta_\delta=\min\{c_*\delta^4/2,g_0/2\}>0. \tag{18}
\]

No compactness of normalized convex fields is used. The quantitative coercivity, strip bound, and affine-observability lemma control arbitrary concentrating fields directly. Normal-dependent fields are included because the proof is applied separately at each actual source facet normal, while all remaining endpoint normals have the same strict profile ceiling.

## 9. Scope

The unique actual deepest source is in the middle fiber, its active directions and ALL menus have been controlled, and (18) bounds the ENTIRE nonnegative normal-dependent convex physical cone. Thus a universal individual-source best-active-menu efficiency at least \(\Gamma_d\) would be false.

Nevertheless \(V/(V+2|D_\delta|)=1/(1+2\alpha)>1/2\) for small \(\delta\). The ordinary centroid of the heavy middle fiber already proves the n=1 OC bound. The example says nothing against a result conditioned on an actual below-OC body minimum, nor against a source-dependent cost allocation whose total is at most the occupied parity budget.

The full proof uses the exact positive-width model and then chooses small h for a fixed explicit geometric parameter. It does not assert that an h=0 active menu automatically covers all h>0 sources, and it does not identify arbitrary cap boundary selectors with limit halfspace indicators.
